method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for social media platforms and online activities
Master relative pronouns qui and que to link ideas in sentences
Use modal verbs (pouvoir, devoir, vouloir) to express ability and obligation online
Build balanced opinions about the advantages and disadvantages of social media
method_card.content:
This lesson covers social media vocabulary, daily online habits and how to give a balanced opinion using relative pronouns (qui/que) and modal verbs.

FrenchEnglish
les réseaux sociauxsocial media / social networks
partagerto share
publier / posterto post / to publish
suivre (quelqu'un)to follow (someone)
un(e) abonné(e)a subscriber / follower
un(e) influenceur / influenceusean influencer
le portable / le smartphonethe mobile phone / smartphone
l'ordinateur (m)the computer
la tablettethe tablet
utileuseful
dangereux / dangereusedangerous
le harcèlement en ligne (Higher)online bullying / cyberbullying
anonyme (Higher)anonymous
virtuel(le) (Higher)virtual

Relative pronouns qui and que: qui replaces the subject of the relative clause (the thing or person doing the action) — it is followed by a verb: C'est un réseau social qui est très populaire. (It is a social network that is very popular.) que (or qu' before a vowel) replaces the object — it is followed by a subject + verb: Le post qu'il a partagé était amusant. (The post that he shared was funny.)

Modal verbs: pouvoir (can), devoir (must), vouloir (to want). They are followed by an infinitive: On peut partager des photos. (You can share photos.) On doit faire attention en ligne. (You must be careful online.) Je veux suivre cet influenceur. (I want to follow this influencer.)

Model paragraph: J'utilise les réseaux sociaux tous les jours. C'est pratique parce qu'on peut communiquer avec des amis qui habitent loin. Cependant, je pense qu'on doit faire attention aux informations qu'on partage en ligne. (I use social media every day. It is practical because you can communicate with friends who live far away. However, I think you must be careful about the information you share online.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — social media and technology appear across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'J'utilise les réseaux sociaux pour partager des photos avec mes amis.'

steps.label: Break it down
steps.content: J'utilise | les réseaux sociaux | pour partager | des photos | avec mes amis.

steps.label: Key vocabulary
steps.content: J'utilise = I use. les réseaux sociaux = social media (note: masculine plural). pour + infinitive = in order to / to. partager = to share.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I use social media to share photos with my friends.

worked_examples.question: Choose qui or que: 'C'est un réseau social ___ beaucoup de gens utilisent.' Which is correct?

steps.label: Check what follows the gap
steps.content: After the gap, we have: beaucoup de gens utilisent — this has its own subject (beaucoup de gens) and verb (utilisent). The pronoun replaces the object of utiliser.

steps.label: Apply the rule
steps.content: qui = subject pronoun (followed by a verb with no new subject). que = object pronoun (followed by a new subject + verb). Here the new subject is beaucoup de gens, so use que.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: C'est un réseau social que beaucoup de gens utilisent. — que because the social network is the object of utiliser.

bronze.question: Match the French social media words to the English meaning
Match the French adjectives and devices to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun
sentence_parts: est très utile pour communiquer. C'est l'application

gaps.correct_explain: qui is the subject pronoun — it replaces the subject of the relative clause and is directly followed by a verb (est).

wrong.que: que is the object pronoun — it is followed by a new subject + verb. Here there is no new subject after the gap, so use qui.

gaps.correct_explain: que is the object pronoun — after the gap we have a new subject (mes amis) + verb (utilisent), so que is correct.

wrong.qui: qui is directly followed by a verb. Here there is a new subject (mes amis) after the gap, so the application is the object — use que.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct modal verb form
sentence_parts: faire attention aux informations qu'on partage. On ne

gaps.correct_explain: doit is the on form of devoir (must / should). On doit = one must / you must.

wrong.peut: peut is the on form of pouvoir (can). The sentence says 'must be careful', so use doit.
wrong.veut: veut is the on form of vouloir (to want). The sentence expresses obligation, so use doit.

gaps.correct_explain: ne ... pas doit → ne doit pas: the negation goes around the modal verb. On ne doit pas + infinitive = one must not ...

wrong.peut: The sentence means 'you must not share your address' — use doit for obligation, not peut (can).

bronze.question: What does 'Je partage des photos sur les réseaux sociaux tous les jours' mean?
options: I share photos on social media every day
I downloaded photos from social media yesterday
I follow people on social media every week
I watched photos on social media every day

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'Social media can be dangerous'?
options: Les réseaux sociaux peuvent être dangereux.
Les réseaux sociaux peuvent être dangereuse.
Les réseaux sociaux peut être dangereux.
Les réseaux sociaux pouvoir être dangereux.

bronze.source_text: Les réseaux sociaux sont utiles mais on doit faire attention. Il y a des personnes qui ne sont pas honnêtes en ligne.
model_answers: Social media is useful but you must be careful. There are people who are not honest online.
Social networks are useful but you must be careful. There are people who are not honest online.
hints: utiles = useful (plural to agree with les réseaux sociaux)
on doit = you must / one must

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
silver.english: Social media which is used badly can be dangerous for young people.
sentence_parts: sont mal utilisés peuvent être dangereux pour les jeunes.

gaps.correct_explain: qui is the subject relative pronoun — it replaces les réseaux sociaux as the subject of sont mal utilisés. It is directly followed by the verb.

wrong.que: que is followed by a new subject + verb. Here the verb (sont) directly follows the pronoun — use qui.
wrong.qu': qu' is used before a vowel or silent h, but it is the object pronoun. Here use the subject pronoun qui.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: C'est une application qui je trouve très utile.
silver.explanation: After the gap, there is a new subject (je) + verb (trouve), so the application is the object. Use que (object pronoun), not qui (subject pronoun).
silver.translation: It is an app that I find very useful.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I follow many influencers who share interesting content.

distractor_labels.que: wrong relative pronoun — qui is needed here because the influencers are the subject of partagent (they share). Que is for the object.

silver.source_text: I think social media can be useful. However, you must not share personal information online.
model_answers: Je pense que les réseaux sociaux peuvent être utiles. Cependant, on ne doit pas partager d'informations personnelles en ligne.
Je trouve que les réseaux sociaux peuvent être utiles. Cependant, on ne doit pas partager d'informations personnelles en ligne.
hints: I think = je pense que / je trouve que
social media = les réseaux sociaux (masculine plural)
you must not = on ne doit pas + infinitive

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: The information that people share on social media is not always reliable.

distractor_labels.qui: wrong relative pronoun — after the gap there is a new subject (les gens) + verb (partagent), so the information is the object — use que not qui
distractor_labels.partage: wrong conjugation — les gens is plural (they), so the verb must be partagent not partage (singular)
distractor_labels.social: wrong form — réseaux sociaux is the fixed plural noun. Do not separate réseaux from sociaux.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are in town and you meet a French exchange student. You have a conversation about social media and online life.

bullets.prompt: Say which social media platforms you use and how often.
bullets.model_answer: J'utilise Instagram et YouTube tous les jours. Je partage des photos et des vidéos avec mes amis.
bullets.note: j'utilise + platform names + tous les jours / toutes les semaines

bullets.prompt: Give one advantage of social media using a relative pronoun.
bullets.model_answer: Les réseaux sociaux ont des avantages — c'est une façon de communiquer avec des amis qui habitent loin.
bullets.note: relative pronoun qui (subject) — the friends are the subject of habitent

bullets.prompt: Give one disadvantage and say what people must not do online.
bullets.model_answer: Cependant, il y a des risques. On ne doit pas partager d'informations personnelles avec des inconnus.
bullets.note: cependant (however) + modal verb: on ne doit pas + infinitive + de after negation

bullets.prompt: Say how long you have been using your smartphone and whether you could live without it.
bullets.model_answer: J'utilise mon smartphone depuis deux ans. Je ne pourrais pas vivre sans lui !
bullets.note: depuis + present tense (j'utilise) + conditional (je ne pourrais pas — I couldn't)

gold.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
gold.english: He posted a video that his followers found very funny.
sentence_parts: ses abonnés ont trouvée très drôle.

gaps.rule: Relative pronoun — object (que) + past participle agreement
gaps.correct_explain: que is the object relative pronoun — after the gap there is a new subject (ses abonnés) + verb (ont trouvée). Note: when que precedes a perfect tense with avoir, the past participle agrees with the noun it replaces — une vidéo (f sg) → trouvée (with -e).

wrong.qui: qui is directly followed by a verb (no new subject). Here there is a new subject ses abonnés, so the video is the object — use que.
